label: paragraph_title
text: A WIFE'S DEBTS.

label: text
text:
HUSBAND IS NOT
LIABLE.

label: text
text: WHEN A

label: text
text: Mr. W. B. Hind's contention that he was not obliged to pay for debts incurred by his wife was upheld yesterday afternoon by Mr. Justice Wood who gave a verdict in his favour in the case in which Lammert Bros. sued for $218 for furniture sold to Mrs. Hind in the sales rooms.

label: text
text: His Honour emphasised that the furniture was delivered to Mrs. Hind at an address other than her own residence for the purpose of furnishing a flat which she proposed to let on her own account. The residence where defendant and his wife were living was already furnished.

label: text
text: THE HIND-LAMMERT CASE:

label: text
text: The law applicable had been stated by Mr. Justice McCardie in a judgment in 1922: "A person who deals with a married woman on credit does so, as far as regards a remedy, against the husband, at his own risk.

label: text
text: In the dispute between the parties no question had arisen of express authority or of authority by estoppel. The plaintiffs, therefore, in order to succeed, had to rely on the presumptive authority arising from cohabitation for the wife to pledge her husband's credit for necessaries.

label: text
text: Continuing. His Honour said marriage in itself did not give a wife authority to pledge her husband's credit. A husband might give express authority to his wife or he might give authority by a coarse of cor. by which he implied conferred authority to contract with one or more persons. After any such authority a wife who is living with her husband, from the fact of conabitation, is held to derive a presumptive authority to contract for her husband but that authority is strictly limited.

label: text
text: Lastly the fact that the plaintiffs were public auctioneers and announced in their printed conditions of sale "cash on delivery," seemed to him to estop them from setting up any presumptive authority in a married woman who might be a successful bidder at a public auction to pledge her husband's credit.

label: text
text: He therefore gave judgment for the defendant.

label: text
text: Mr. Hind, who appeared yesterday and at the hearing for himself as defendant, said he had already agreed with his friend to pay for the articles in question. He had contested the case purely and simply as a matter of principle.

label: text
text: CHINA LIGHT METER READER "SACKED."

label: text
text:
A cousin failing to pay in a $10 "deposit" to the China Light & Power Co., Ltd., because he could not find the address led to the relative—a meter reader—being bound over for six months at the Kowloon Police Court yesterday.
Defendant had taken the money, without authority, from a Chinese woman. His cousin produced the sum in court. Mr. W. J. Brown said that defendant would be dismissed. In the circumstances Mr. E. W. Hamilton was satisfied with a bond.

label: text
text: KOWLOON UNION CHURCH PROGRESS.

label: text
text: ANNUAL MEETING ITEMS:

label: text
text: At the annual meeting of the Kowloon Union Church last night, the Rev. J. Kirk Maconachie (Hongkong pastor) said that today nobody would say they had been ahead of time as it had become more evident that the church was greatly needed.

label: text
text:
The Rev. J. Horace Johnston, B.A., presided over a large attendance of the congregation.
Mr. C. Wallace, the hon. treasurer, reported an increased balance, viz., $731.74.

label: text
text: Items in the report of the hon secretary, Mr. D. J. Purves were:—

label: text
text: Great advance on attendance at services since 1924.

label: text
text: Many improvements and additions to Church and grounds.

label: text
text: Mr. Andrews replaced Mrs. Craig as organist, & presentation

label: text
text: having been made to the latter. Mr. Fleming took the place of Captain Davies as choirmaster.

label: text
text: Collections have been most liberal; special thankofferings at the anniversary making up for lean strike months.

label: text
text: In the New Year the minister gave a party to children on his own outlay. A social sub-committee was appointed in January; a gathering was held in March and another in November. Weekly bathing picnics were held till the strike intervene. $85.80 was realised for a crockery account. The committee recommends a monthly social event.

label: text
text: Thanks are expressed to Sunday school workers, attendance having increased from 25 to 45.

label: text
text: Five marriages and eight baptisms had been performed and 100 names were on the communion role.

label: text
text: The Rev. Mr. Maconachie presented to the Church a bible purchased at Home.

label: text
text: Officers elected were:—

label: text
text: Gentlemen—Messrs. Arnott, D. Gow, J. Cameron, W. McFarlane, D. F. Warren, E. C. Tregilles, J. Smith, D. J. Purves.

label: text
text: Ladies—Mrs. J. A. Craig, Mrs. D. Davies, Mrs. Dick, Mrs. D. F. Warren, Mrs. D. M. Nelson, Miss Farrell.

label: text
text: ENQUIRY INTO SERGEANT BLACKMAN'S DEATH

label: text
text: SHVENUM COLLECTING "WORRIES."

label: text
text: Evidence was given at the inquiry yesterday into the death of Sergt. Blackman that the deceased had been ill on and off for several days before the night in the course of which the evidence points to his having shot himself. On that actual night (December 2) a Northern dialect interpreter deposed to seeing him at eight o'clock when witness went to ask him for the revolver for the patrol. The Sergt. said he was very ill but said he would see how he felt in the morning before going to hospital.

label: text
text:
Witness put his hand on the Sergeant's head and found it very hot. He felt his cheek and it was "hot like fire." Witness was not awakened during the night and he did not hear a shot fired. The next morning Sergt. Blackman's boy made a report that the Sergeant had been found dead in bed with a shot wound in his head.
Witness added that Sergeant Blackman had a certain amount of revenue to collect from the distillery. On the night of his death there were over $500 of revenue money in the safe.

label: text
text: Mr. Lindsell: Did he like collecting Government money?

label: text
text:
lecting Government money?
Witness: No. He said that it was not Police work, and that it should be collected by the Revenue Officers.

label: text
text: In answer to further questions witness said that collecting the revenue money seemed to worry him. He was the only European at the station, but now there were two European officers.

label: text
text:
Another Chinese interpreter, asked if he heard a shot, said that no one did. The night was windy and the wind made a noise in the trees near the station.
Dr. E. P. Minett, Government Bacteriologist and Officer in charge of Mortuaries, gave evidence as to the nature of the wound. The point of the entry of the bullet was charred at the edges. The bullet had gone clean through, the position of the two wounds being consistent with the wound having been self-inflicted. Dr. Minett added that examination of the body had revealed signs of advanced tuberculosis.

label: text
text: In reply to a question by Mr. Lindsell, Mr. Gerrard intimated that he would make inquiries to discover if Sergeant Blackman had been medically attended during the past few months, and if he had been in hospital during the past year.

label: text
text: At this stage the inquiry was adjourned until next Thursday at 2.15 p.m.

label: paragraph_title
text: “RED” PARTNER.

label: text
text: MANAGER CHARGED WITH $370 THEFT.

label: text
text: Involving his tenureship of a "red" share (the owner of which, as recognised in law, is a person who is not entitled to interest on capital but who shares with the partners the surplus profit after payment of interest on capital), the manager of a Chinese rice firm was charged before Mr. E. W. Hamilton at the Kowloon Magistracy yesterday with the theft of $370 belonging to the firm.

label: text
text: Complainant (wife of the sole proprietor) alleged that she paid defendant $370 for settlement of an urgent account and purchase of stock. According to evidence he vanished after receiving the money but returned on three days when the master's wife was not there. On November 28 he attempted to take away the books but was arrested on the mistress's initiative.
